quizName: DMV Practice Test #7 25 Questions • Passing Score 21

questions.question: Which colors help riders be seen the best?

options.text: Orange and red
Green and blue
Purple and gold
Black and white

questions.correctAnswerText: Orange and red
questions.explanation: Bright orange, red, yellow, or green clothing makes you most visible to other drivers.

questions.question: A person drinks 7 alcoholic drinks in 3 hours. The body removes about 1 drink per hour. How many drinks will likely remain in their system 3 hours after their last drink?

options.text: Two
Three
Four
Five

questions.correctAnswerText: Four
questions.explanation: Subtract the number of hours since the last drink from the total drinks consumed. 7 drinks minus 3 hours of removal equals 4 drinks remaining.

questions.question: After mounting your motorcycle, which should you NOT do?

options.text: Clean the mirrors
Check that the horn works
Close the fuel supply valve
Check that the clutch works smoothly

questions.correctAnswerText: Close the fuel supply valve
questions.explanation: After mounting, check that the clutch, throttle, horn, and brakes work. Clean the mirrors. Keep the fuel supply valve open.

questions.question: Which is NOT a purpose of choosing a good lane position?

options.text: Avoid road hazards
Stay out of other drivers' blind spots
Avoid being seen by other drivers
Make yourself more visible to others

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid being seen by other drivers
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see and be seen. It keeps you out of blind spots, helps you avoid hazards, protects your lane, communicates your intentions, avoids wind blasts, and gives you an escape route.

questions.question: What is an advantage of keeping space between your motorcycle and other vehicles?

options.text: You can pass danger more quickly
You have a narrower view so you stay focused
You have more time to react to what others do
You can follow the next vehicle's path more easily

questions.correctAnswerText: You have more time to react to what others do
questions.explanation: Space between vehicles gives you a clearer view of hazards, more time to react, and more room to move around dangers.

questions.question: What should a good lane position do?

options.text: Keep you out of other drivers' blind spots
Give you a good view of the shoulder
Give you a poor view of road hazards
Invite other drivers to share your lane

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep you out of other drivers' blind spots
questions.explanation: Choose a lane position that helps you see others and be seen. Do not stay in another driver's blind spot for long.

questions.question: Why should motorcyclists in a group avoid riding in pairs?

options.text: A merging driver may not see both riders
Helmet reflections may make it hard for riders to see
Riding in pairs leaves no room to maneuver around hazards
It is too hard for left-side riders to exit the highway

questions.correctAnswerText: Riding in pairs leaves no room to maneuver around hazards
questions.explanation: When riding in a group, do not ride in pairs. Neither rider will have enough space to move and avoid dangers.

questions.question: What is the best way to stop quickly?

options.text: Use the front brake only
Use the front brake first
Ease off the throttle and use the front brake
Use both brakes at the same time

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both brakes at the same time
questions.explanation: To stop quickly, apply both the front and rear brakes together.

questions.question: Where is the front brake lever located?

options.text: On the left handgrip
On the right handgrip
By the left foot peg
By the right foot peg

questions.correctAnswerText: On the right handgrip
questions.explanation: The front brake lever is on the right handgrip. Know where all your motorcycle's controls are before you ride.

questions.question: How much of a motorcycle's braking power comes from the front brake?

options.text: 10 percent
25 percent
50 percent
75 percent

questions.correctAnswerText: 75 percent
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides about three-quarters of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: Where is the throttle usually located?

options.text: Near the left footrest
Near the right footrest
On the left handle grip
On the right handle grip

questions.correctAnswerText: On the right handle grip
questions.explanation: The throttle is on the right handle grip. Learn where all your motorcycle controls are before you ride.

questions.question: How often should a motorcycle rider check their mirrors?

options.text: Never
Occasionally
Frequently
More often than the amount time spent looking ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: Frequently
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors frequently. This helps you see hazards behind you.

questions.question: If you are not going slow enough when shifting into a lower gear, what happens?

options.text: The motorcycle could lurch and the rear tire could skid.
The motorcycle could accelerate too quickly.
The front tire will likely skid.
The engine will make a loud noise.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle could lurch and the rear tire could skid.
questions.explanation: If you shift into a lower gear while going too fast, the motorcycle will lurch and the rear wheel may skid.

questions.question: Why is riding directly alongside another vehicle discouraged?

options.text: You may have a hard time getting to a highway exit.
You may be in the other vehicle's blind spot.
You may block the driver's view.
It prevents other drivers from passing both of you.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may be in the other vehicle's blind spot.
questions.explanation: Riding alongside another vehicle is dangerous because you could be in the vehicle's blind spot. The driver may turn into your lane without seeing you. The vehicle also blocks your escape route if a hazard appears.

questions.question: What should you do to reduce your chances of a crash?

options.text: Do not use your turn signals when changing lanes.
Follow other vehicles closely.
Watch about five feet ahead of your motorcycle while riding.
Always be ready to use crash-avoidance techniques.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always be ready to use crash-avoidance techniques.
questions.explanation: To reduce crash risk, be visible to other drivers. Use turn signals, your brake light, and good lane position. Keep space around your motorcycle and look ahead, behind, and beside your vehicle. Always be ready to avoid a hazard.

questions.question: Which body part operates the gearshift lever?

options.text: Your right hand.
Your right foot.
Your left hand.
Your left foot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your left foot.
questions.explanation: The gearshift lever is in front of the left footrest. You operate it with your left foot.

questions.question: What does a plastic, shatter-resistant face shield do?

options.text: It is not necessary if you have a windshield.
It only protects your eyes.
It helps protect your whole face.
It does not protect your face as well as goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: It helps protect your whole face.
questions.explanation: A face shield protects your whole face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield does not replace a face shield or goggles.

questions.question: What is engine braking?

options.text: It is illegal.
It is slowing down by turning the engine off.
It is slowing down by downshifting.
It is not encouraged because it damages the engine.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is slowing down by downshifting.
questions.explanation: Downshifting slows your motorcycle like brakes do. This is called engine braking.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection, what should you do?

options.text: Assume other drivers see you, especially if they make eye contact.
Never assume other drivers see you.
Stay focused on moving through the intersection.
Speed up to make others notice you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never assume other drivers see you.
questions.explanation: Never assume that other drivers see you, even if they look at you. Drivers often look directly at motorcycles but do not notice them. Always slow down when approaching an intersection.

questions.question: If you must ride over an obstacle, what should you do?

options.text: Decrease your speed as much as possible.
Lean the motorcycle to one side.
Speed up, if possible.
Stay on your seat and remove your feet from the footrests.

questions.correctAnswerText: Decrease your speed as much as possible.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid an obstacle, slow down and approach it at a 90-degree angle if possible. Keep your motorcycle straight up. Just before you hit it, ease off the throttle to lighten the front wheel.

questions.question: In general, riders should:

options.text: Pick one lane position and always use it.
Change lane positions frequently to prevent boredom.
Choose a lane position that gives them the most space around them.
Never use the center lane position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Choose a lane position that gives them the most space around them.
questions.explanation: Road and traffic conditions change all the time. The safest lane position also changes. Pick the position that gives you the most space around you and makes it easiest for other drivers to see you.

questions.question: You should increase your following distance if:

options.text: The pavement is dry.
The pavement is wet.
You can see through the vehicle ahead of you.
The sun is out.

questions.correctAnswerText: The pavement is wet.
questions.explanation: You need more space around you if your motorcycle takes longer to stop. This includes wet pavement, when you cannot see through the vehicle ahead, or when traffic is heavy and another driver might pull in front of you. Keep a larger distance between you and the vehicle ahead.

questions.question: One way to tell if your rear tire has gone flat while riding is if:

options.text: There is a hissing noise coming from the rear of the bike.
The back end jerks from side to side.
You cannot speed up.
The rear brake stops working.

questions.correctAnswerText: The back end jerks from side to side.
questions.explanation: When your rear tire fails, the back of your motorcycle will jerk from side to side. You usually will not hear a tire fail.

questions.question: Usually, a good way to handle a tailgater is to:

options.text: Move onto the shoulder to get out of their way.
Speed up to put distance between you and the tailgater.
Ignore them.
Change lanes and let them pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle a tailgater is usually to get them in front of you. If you can do it safely, change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up only makes danger worse by encouraging them to follow you faster.

questions.question: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield:

options.text: Is not necessary if you have a windshield.
Only protects your eyes.
Helps protect your whole face.
Does not protect your face as well as goggles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Helps protect your whole face.
questions.explanation: A plastic, shatter-resistant face shield protects your entire face in a crash. Goggles only protect your eyes. A windshield does not protect your face as well as a face shield or goggles.
